title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: MuleSoft Anypoint
providers.scope_notes: Covers MuleSoft Anypoint Platform. Anypoint Platform control plane (US/EU/Gov); IP allowlist only US/EU commercial; audit export needs Anypoint Integration Advanced or Titanium.

controls.name: Revoke API contract
controls.what: Blocks a client application from calling the API instance.
controls.setting: API Manager > API instance > Contracts > Revoke

controls.name: Contract approval
controls.what: Instance owner approves access requests before credentials work against the API.

controls.name: IP Allowlist policy
controls.what: Gateway policy that only lets listed IPs or ranges call a managed API instance.
controls.setting: API Manager > API instance > Policies > IP Allowlist

controls_unknown: Whether IP allowlist applies to connected app token requests or API calls with an issued token
Whether deleting a client-credentials app or rotating its secret invalidates unexpired access tokens
Whether a client-credentials app's tokens can be revoked without deleting it (Revoke Authorization is documented for user authorizations)
Exact UI setting name for disabling connected apps org-wide
Whether read/GET API calls are audit logged
Environment client secret rotation procedure (help.salesforce.com KB 001115221 did not render)
Whether IdP conditional access applies to connected app tokens (not stated)

auth_paths.name: API client application credentials (client ID / secret for API instances)

authentication.summary: Client applications registered in Exchange get a client ID and optional secret to call customer APIs protected by a client ID enforcement policy. These authenticate to customer APIs, not to Anypoint Platform APIs.

federation.details: Static credentials; external client providers (e.g. Entra ID, PingFederate) can be used instead.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only if the API owner applies the IP Allowlist policy to the API instance; applies to calls to that API, not platform-wide.

renewal.summary: Secret reusable; reset is an audited action.

administration.summary: API instance owner approves access requests (contracts) and can revoke, restore, or delete contracts in API Manager.
administration.conditions: Root org Organization Administrator for revoke/delete.

inventory.details: API Manager > API instance > Contracts lists contracts per instance; not all clients appear in the UI, and GET /accounts/api/organizations/{orgId}/clients is documented for the org-wide client count.

disable.ui: API Manager > (API instance) > SLA tiers: set tier to manual approval; then API Manager > API Administration > (instance) > Contracts > Approve / Reject

log_sources.name: Anypoint Platform audit log (Access Management > Audit Log, Audit Log Query API)
log_sources.notes: Default retention 1 year (6 years for orgs before 2023-07-10), configurable 30-2190 days; export via Telemetry Exporter needs Anypoint Integration Advanced or Titanium.

anomaly_cues: Contract requests or tier changes for sensitive API instances

containment.steps: Revoke the contract in API Manager, then reset secret or delete the app.
containment.notes: Revoke blocks the client app from the API.

unknown: Gateway-side request logging depends on customer runtime
Calls depend on the customer's own APIs
